source.title: Heavy-Tailed Universality Predicts Trends in Test Accuracies for Very Large Pre-Trained Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Charles H. Martin; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures weight-matrix capacity metrics and compares them with reported test accuracy across pretrained models. It does not test the interventions or specific properties in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study reports per-model values for weighted average PL exponent α̂ and Top1 accuracy in Tables 1–3, and discusses average log Frobenius norm against accuracy in figures. These bear on the broad claim that measured properties of trained networks track generalization, but none measures the training-to-test gap or a property named by V1–V8. It also cites prior work; cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates spectral power-law and Frobenius-norm metrics against reported accuracy of pretrained ImageNet models. None measures a claim version: in particular, these metrics are not magnitude-aware sharpness, and reported test accuracy alone does not establish the generalization gap in V7. Width variants do not establish V2 because training error and the interpolation threshold are unreported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that weighted spectral power-law exponents predict reported test-accuracy trends within many pretrained architecture series, and connect this metric approximately to the average log squared Frobenius norm. They acknowledge counterexamples. They do not establish magnitude-aware sharpness effects or training-to-test gap prediction.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes existing pretrained ImageNet models without retraining; measures weight-matrix spectra and compares metrics with reported test accuracies. This differs from the original claim versions' training and intervention comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture series; the reported association has exceptions in DenseNet, ResNeXt, MeNet, and FDMobileNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Within many pretrained ImageNet architecture series, lower weighted spectral power-law metric α̂ accompanies higher reported Top1 accuracy. The average log Frobenius norm also tracks accuracy for VGG and ResNet, with additional outliers. ResNeXt and FDMobileNet show the opposite metric trend; MeNet has no discernible pattern. These are associations with test accuracy, without measurements of sharpness or training-to-test gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-spectrum and norm metrics can track reported test-accuracy trends within many pretrained image-classification architecture families, with architecture-dependent exceptions.

record.problems: The study uses reported test accuracies from existing pretrained models and does not report their training errors, so it cannot assess train-test gaps. Accuracy is not reevaluated on a common test set in this text. The authors identify counterexample architectures; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the metric-accuracy associations.
record.rows_left_out: Two Table 3 results omitted to stay within 60 rows: fdmobilenet_w1 and the final MeNet entry alignment is not safely recoverable from the flattened table; the table lists 12 counterexample model names and values, while only 11 paired value entries are legible in the supplied text. The exact affected entries are not assigned rather than guessing.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width achieving zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training-to-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain unlinked to V1–V8; cannot_determine describes their inability to measure those versions, not uncertainty that the reported accuracies exist. The rows_left_out explanation is incorrect: Table 3 contains all 12 counterexample value pairs, all seven MeNet models are already recorded, and only fdmobilenet_w1 is omitted (Top1 65.30, α̂ 7.10). It bears on no listed version. Several prose directions conflict with the tables: ResNet generally has lower metrics at higher accuracy; ResNeXt and FDMobileNet have higher α̂ at higher accuracy. SqueezeNet's two tabulated points also run opposite to the proposed relationship despite its placement among working examples.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures; the study instead evaluates PL-exponent and Frobenius-norm metrics.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
